title: A Multilingual Perspective on Probing Gender Bias
findings: Across all models tested, religious identities led to the most pronounced disparate treatment compared to other categories like gender, nationality, and disability. Certain identities, particularly Muslims and Jews, face disproportionate levels of stereotypical associations. The most frequently occurring shared stereotype within the religion category was related to starvation. Larger model variants were found to exhibit a higher degree of bias.
